title: RAW UNREVIEWED: table-to-prose copying preserves omitted-header scope across row switches
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. A compiler copying a table into prose may omit repeated headers while retaining row keys and dependent cell order. An independently bound table schema would predict exactly where a new row key changes the scope of subsequent cells, distinguishing a repeated participant name from a column property or inherited header. No four-column, numeric or astronomical schema is presumed.

design.mechanism: A bounded historical copying procedure linearizes rows and suppresses repeated headers with explicit scope retention.
design.unit: Complete externally attested source table and its known prose redaction, followed only after selection by complete admitted target entries.
design.contrast: Row-wise inherited-header copying versus column-wise copying and independently written prose under the same fixed spelling model.
design.prediction: Changing a row key changes the owner of subsequent cell values but not their column roles; a retained header controls multiple unequal values and its scope ends at the next independently bound row boundary. Whole-entry assignments must satisfy every occupied and empty source cell.
design.scope: RAW proposal; no source-target binding supplied. GDT273 position/record-size baseline and closed ZODIAC_AND_ASTRONOMICAL_DICTIONARIES retained. Requires authorial coordinate/order or independently owned schema before target matching; cannot rescue serialized circular maps by choosing a new rotation. IDEA120/121 source montage is related, but this adds explicit row-header inheritance and empty-cell consequences. No arbitrary meanings or target access.
